grammar.title: Infinitive of Purpose (I went out to buy milk)
grammar.explanation:
We use **to + verb** to say **why** we do something. *I went to the shop **to buy** some milk* answers the question *Why?*

This is called the **infinitive of purpose**. *She is learning English **to get** a better job.*

Before a noun, use **for + noun**, not **to**. *We went to the café **for** a coffee*, but *We went to the café **to drink** a coffee.*

Do not use **for** before a verb. Say *I came here **to see** you*, never *for see* or *for to see*.

**In order to** and **so as to** mean the same as **to**, but they are more formal. *They studied hard **in order to** pass the exam.*

For a negative purpose, use **in order not to** or **so as not to**. *Speak quietly **so as not to** wake the baby.*

In our **block of flats**, I go to the **bathroom** **to brush** my teeth. At night, I take a **bath** **to feel** calm, and I do not **bother** to cook late.
examples: *I went to the bakery **to buy** some bread.* (to + verb)
*We went to the café **for** a coffee.* (for + noun)
*He called me **to ask** about the meeting.* (to + verb)
*They studied hard **in order to** pass the exam.* (formal)
*Close the window **so as not to** let the cold in.* (negative purpose)

practice.q: Rewrite using to + verb: I went to the bathroom because I wanted to brush my teeth.
practice.a: I went to the bathroom to brush my teeth.

practice.q: Rewrite using to + verb: She takes a bath because she wants to feel calm.
practice.a: She takes a bath to feel calm.

practice.q: Rewrite using for + noun: I went out because I wanted some food.
practice.a: I went out for some food.

practice.q: Rewrite using in order not to: People in the block of flats speak quietly because they do not want to wake the baby.
practice.a: People in the block of flats speak quietly in order not to wake the baby.
